subject: Media Literacy
title: How Images Shape Public Opinion
description: A short lesson to help you apply How Images Shape Public Opinion.

hook.text: The same protest photographed from two angles looks either massive or tiny. Both photos are 'real.'

buildup.text: Images shape opinion not just through manipulation but through selection — which moment is captured matters.

discovery.text: Photo editors choose which image runs with a story. That choice frames the entire narrative.

twist.text: A politician photographed while blinking looks confused. Photographed while gesturing, they look powerful. Same person, same day.

climax.text: You don't need to alter an image to manipulate with it. You just need to choose the right one.

punchline.text: The camera doesn't lie. But the person choosing the photo might.

quiz.question: How can unaltered photos still be used to manipulate?
options: They can't — unaltered photos are always honest
Through selective choice of which moment to capture and publish
